title: Set the light
scenario: A café wants a photo-style image of a steaming mug of cocoa on a wooden table for its evening menu. The owner keeps saying it should feel “cosy” — which, as written, is a feeling rather than an instruction.
task: Fill the three light slots — direction, quality and time of day — so the mood comes from the light instead of from adjectives.

fields.label: Direction (where the light comes from)
fields.placeholder: Low light from the right, pooling across the table…

fields.label: Quality (soft or hard, and from what kind of source)
fields.placeholder: Soft and diffused, like a shaded table lamp…

fields.label: Time and colour (when it reads as, and how warm or cool)
fields.placeholder: Evening: warm amber glow, deep soft shadows…

hints: Adjectives describe the goal — the slots describe what to render. “Cosy” is the outcome, not the instruction.
One source, one direction. Light “from everywhere” renders as no light at all.
explanation: The three light dials turn “make it cosy” into renderable decisions: a low lamp on one side, a soft diffused source, evening warmth. Because each dial is separate, you can fix a wrong mood by changing one of them — swap the amber for cool daylight and the same scene reads as a crisp morning. Adjectives leave the model guessing; light slots leave it nothing to guess.
sampleSolution: Direction: low light from the right, pooling across the wooden table and falling on the mug. Quality: soft and diffused — the glow of a shaded table lamp with gentle transitions and no hard edges. Time and colour: evening, warm amber, deep soft shadows stretching to the left.
